Photos go in. Open a project, drop your photos or folders anywhere in the window, and galleryLAB starts
importing straight away.

## Download

- **galleryLAB-setup.exe** installs galleryLAB for your Windows account, over an existing copy in the same
  folder. If you have 0.1.1 or later, galleryLAB installs this update by itself.
- **galleryLAB-portable.exe** runs without installing and replaces itself when a new version comes out.

Requires Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The build isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may say it
“protected your PC”; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## What's new

- **Open a project** by clicking it in the Library (or Enter on the keyboard). **Library** or Escape goes back.
- **Drop photos or folders anywhere in the window** to import them, or use **Add photos** and **Add folder**.
  Folders are read all the way down, and their structure is kept inside the project.
- **The contact sheet fills in as you watch.** The first thumbnails appear within a couple of seconds; the
  rest follow while the import continues. Nothing covers or tints a photo.
- **One calm progress line** with Pause, Resume and Cancel, and an **Issues** list that says plainly why a file
  couldn't be imported (with Retry where it can help). Duplicates are skipped and counted, never copied twice.
- **Formats:** JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF (8 and 16-bit) and HEIC. Files are recognised by their contents,
  not their name. RAW files aren't supported yet; export them as JPEG or TIFF and add them again.
- **Metadata** (camera, lens, exposure, capture time, GPS, rating, title, caption, keywords) is read and kept.
- **Originals are never touched.** Copies go into the project's `originals` folder; everything derived lives
  in `.gallery` and can be rebuilt.
- **Quit any time.** An import that is interrupted picks up where it stopped the next time the project opens,
  with no duplicates. The Library card shows the import's progress.
